## Model
model: @UNETLoader.unet_name = minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors # The MiniMax H3 model or checkpoint
shift_video: int = 12 # Sigma shift for the video. Higher spends more of the steps at high noise (composition and motion), lower more on fine detail.
shift_audio: int = 3 # Sigma shift for the audio, like shift_video.
## Optimization
attention: choice pytorch, sage, comfy_kitchen = pytorch # The attention backend. pytorch: ComfyUI's default. sage: SageAttention through KJNodes (needs the sageattention package). comfy_kitchen: ComfyUI's comfy-kitchen kernels.
sparse_attention: choice none, vsa # vsa: block-sparse attention (the core Model Sparse Attention node, set up inside H3 Model Optimization). Faster on long or large videos, at some cost in detail. none: full attention.
spectrum: bool = false # Spectrum (xmarre's pack): forecasts part of the model's work on some steps instead of computing it. Faster, at a small cost in quality.
turbo_loader: choice off, normal, larryvrh = off # How a turbo (few-step) LoRA is applied. off: no turbo LoRA. normal: ComfyUI's LoRA loader, for LoRAs such as LightX2V. larryvrh: Larryvrh's MiniMax-H3 Turbo loader, for its own turbo LoRA.
turbo_lora: @LoraName (obvpm).lora_name when turbo_loader != off # The turbo LoRA file. It must suit the loader chosen above.
turbo_strength: float 0..1.00 = 1.0 when turbo_loader != off # The turbo LoRA's strength. 1.0 is as trained.
## Sampling
sampler: @SamplerName (obvpm).sampler_name = euler # The sampler.
## Schedule
steps: int = 20 # Sampling steps. With a turbo LoRA, the step count it was made for; without one, about 20. Step ranges and x steps are counted in these.
scheduler: @SchedulerName (obvpm).scheduler = beta # The noise schedule.
dual_stage: bool = false # Generate in two stages: the first at first_stage_scale of the size, its result latent-upscaled to the full size, then a second stage that finishes it there. Composition and motion are settled cheaply at the small size, the detail at the full size. Generation only: an upscale's refine ignores it.
schedule: choice full, first_x_steps, last_x_steps, step_range, manual = full when dual_stage = false # The sigmas the sampler runs. full: the scheduler's whole curve. first_x_steps / last_x_steps: only the first or the last x steps of it. step_range: steps from_step to to_step. manual: the sigmas typed below.
refine_amount: float 0..1.00 = 1.0 # Upscale only (switched off on the generation settings): how much of the upscaled video is generated again, the refine's denoise; 1.0 = the whole curve, as for a generation. It shapes the curve first -- the refine runs the last part of a longer schedule -- and the schedule choice cuts from that. Low keeps it close to the upscale; higher adds more new detail but can change faces and motion.
x_steps: int 1..200 = 4 when schedule = first_x_steps, last_x_steps # How many steps of the curve to run.
from_step: int 1..200 = 1 when schedule = step_range # The first step to run, 1 = the first. With 16 steps, 9 to 16 runs the second half.
to_step: int 1..200 = 4 when schedule = step_range # The last step to run (itself included).
sigmas: text = 1.0, 0.988, 0.973, 0.952, 0.923, 0.878, 0.8, 0.632, 0.0 when schedule = manual # The sigmas to run, from high to low, separated by commas. The default is shift 12's simple schedule in 8 steps.
extra_steps: int 0..16 = 0 when dual_stage = false # Split the last step into this many more equal steps: 0.235 -> 0 with 1 runs 0.235 -> 0.118 -> 0. Typed sigmas are left as typed.
## First stage
first_stage_scale: float 0.25..1.00 = 0.5 when dual_stage = true # The first stage's width and height as a fraction of the video's, rounded to 32 pixels. 0.5 is the latent upscaler's own 2x (1376 x 768 starts at 704 x 384); 0.7 is about half the pixels.
first_stage_schedule: choice full, first_x_steps, last_x_steps, step_range, manual = first_x_steps when dual_stage = true # The sigmas the first stage runs, before the latent upscale (choices as for schedule). Usually first_x_steps.
first_stage_x_steps: int 1..200 = 4 when first_stage_schedule = first_x_steps, last_x_steps # Steps the first stage runs. 4 of 8 is the first half of the curve.
first_stage_from_step: int 1..200 = 1 when first_stage_schedule = step_range # The first step the first stage runs, 1 = the first.
first_stage_to_step: int 1..200 = 4 when first_stage_schedule = step_range # The last step the first stage runs (itself included).
first_stage_sigmas: text = 1.0, 0.988, 0.973, 0.952, 0.923 when first_stage_schedule = manual # The first stage's sigmas, from high to low.
first_stage_extra_steps: int 0..16 = 0 when dual_stage = true # Split the first stage's last step into this many more equal steps.
## Second stage
second_stage_schedule: choice full, first_x_steps, last_x_steps, step_range, manual = last_x_steps when dual_stage = true # The sigmas the second stage runs at the full size, after the latent upscale (choices as for schedule). Usually last_x_steps or a step_range that starts where the first stage stopped; full starts again from pure noise and throws the first stage away.
second_stage_x_steps: int 1..200 = 4 when second_stage_schedule = first_x_steps, last_x_steps # Steps the second stage runs, at the end of the curve. More steps start it noisier: more detail of its own, less of the first stage kept.
second_stage_from_step: int 1..200 = 5 when second_stage_schedule = step_range # The first step the second stage runs. With 16 steps, 5 to 8 leaves 9-16 to the upscale's refine.
second_stage_to_step: int 1..200 = 8 when second_stage_schedule = step_range # The last step the second stage runs (itself included).
second_stage_sigmas: text = 0.923, 0.878, 0.8, 0.632, 0.0 when second_stage_schedule = manual # The second stage's sigmas, from high to low. Start where the first stage stopped, or higher to re-noise more of it.
second_stage_extra_steps: int 0..16 = 0 when dual_stage = true # Split the second stage's last step into this many more equal steps.

hq_format: @H3JointRenderPro.hq_format = off # Also save the finished upscale in a high quality format, from the same decoded frames at 16 bits per channel. h265: a small, widely playable master. av1: the smallest file for its quality (slow). prores: for editing (.mov). ffv1: lossless archive (.mkv). off: only the H.264 take.
hq_filename_prefix: text = upscale_hq when hq_format != off # Filename prefix for the high quality copy, within base_folder.
h265_crf: int 0..51 = 12 when hq_format = h265 # H.265 quality (CRF): lower is better and bigger. 12 keeps fine detail; 18-22 is typical for sharing.
h265_preset: @H3JointRenderPro.h265_preset = slow when hq_format = h265 # x265 speed: slower presets make a smaller file at the same quality, and take longer.
h265_bit_depth: @H3JointRenderPro.h265_bit_depth = 10-bit when hq_format = h265 # 10-bit avoids banding in gradients (skies, shadows). 8-bit only for old players and TVs.
h265_tune: @H3JointRenderPro.h265_tune = none when hq_format = h265 # grain keeps fine noise and texture instead of smoothing it away (a bigger file).
av1_crf: int 0..63 = 14 when hq_format = av1 # AV1 quality (CRF): lower is better and bigger. 14 keeps fine detail; 25-35 is typical for streaming.
av1_preset: int 2..8 = 5 when hq_format = av1 # SVT-AV1 speed: 2 is slowest and best, 8 fast. AV1 at these settings is the slowest format by far.
av1_tune: @H3JointRenderPro.av1_tune = visual quality when hq_format = av1 # visual quality keeps texture the eye notices; psnr optimises a metric and looks softer.
av1_bit_depth: @H3JointRenderPro.av1_bit_depth = 10-bit when hq_format = av1 # 10-bit avoids banding in gradients. 8-bit only for old players.
prores_profile: @H3JointRenderPro.prores_profile = hq when hq_format = prores # ProRes flavour, smallest to largest: proxy, lt, standard, hq (the usual master), 4444 and 4444 xq (full colour resolution, 4:4:4).
ffv1_pixel_format: @H3JointRenderPro.ffv1_pixel_format = rgb 16-bit when hq_format = ffv1 # rgb 16-bit stores the decoded frames exactly; yuv 4:4:4 10-bit is about half the size and visually lossless.

nodes.title: Two-Stage Generation
widgets_values:
**Two-stage generation**

Turn on `dual_stage` in **H3 Generation Engine Settings**, or pick the *lightx2v dual stage* preset. The first stage samples the start of the schedule at `first_stage_scale` of the size, the latent upscaler takes it to the full size, and the second stage finishes it there. Extends still join their clip exactly: the second stage pins the clip's own latents.

With `dual_stage` off nothing in this group runs.
